ml-framework.prompt: Training error is low and validation error is much higher. What is the model doing?
ml-framework.explanation: A large generalization gap is the signature of high variance; regularize, simplify or add data.

ml-framework.prompt: In the bias–variance decomposition, which term can no model remove?
ml-framework.explanation: Noise in the targets limits any predictor, however good.
options: The irreducible noise σ2\sigma^2σ2
None; all can be removed with enough data

ml-framework.prompt: Which actions mainly reduce variance? (select all)
ml-framework.explanation: Flexibility lowers bias but raises variance; the others reduce variance.

ml-framework.prompt: What is the difference between a parameter and a hyperparameter?
ml-framework.explanation: Weights are parameters; tree depth, learning rate and regularization strength are hyperparameters tuned on validation data.
options: Parameters are learned from data; hyperparameters are chosen before or around training
Hyperparameters are learned; parameters are fixed
Parameters only exist in neural networks

linear-regression.prompt: What is the closed-form least-squares solution?
linear-regression.explanation: Setting the gradient −2X⊤(y−Xw)-2\mathbf X^\top(\mathbf y-\mathbf X\mathbf w)−2X⊤(y−Xw) to zero gives the normal equations.
options: w^=X⊤y\hat{\mathbf w}=\mathbf X^\top\mathbf yw^=X⊤y
w^=(X⊤X)−1X⊤y\hat{\mathbf w}=(\mathbf X^\top\mathbf X)^{-1}\mathbf X^\top\mathbf yw^=(X⊤X)−1X⊤y
w^=X−1y\hat{\mathbf w}=\mathbf X^{-1}\mathbf yw^=X−1y
w^=(XX⊤)−1y\hat{\mathbf w}=(\mathbf X\mathbf X^\top)^{-1}\mathbf yw^=(XX⊤)−1y

linear-regression.prompt: Why does lasso (L1) produce exactly-zero weights while ridge (L2) does not?
linear-regression.explanation: The diamond-shaped L1 ball touches the loss contours at a corner, setting some coordinates to zero: automatic feature selection.
options: The L1 constraint region has corners on the axes where the optimum often lands

linear-regression.prompt: The least-squares residual vector is orthogonal to every column of X\mathbf XX.
linear-regression.explanation: The normal equations say exactly X⊤(y−Xw^)=0\mathbf X^\top(\mathbf y-\mathbf X\hat{\mathbf w})=\mathbf 0X⊤(y−Xw^)=0.

linear-regression.prompt: Linear regression can fit a parabola if you add x2x^2x2 as a feature.
linear-regression.explanation: It is linear in the weights, not in the inputs, so nonlinear features give nonlinear fits.

logistic-regression.prompt: What is the gradient of the softmax cross-entropy loss with respect to the logits z\mathbf zz?
logistic-regression.explanation: Prediction minus one-hot target: the same simple form as linear regression's gradient.
options: y−p\mathbf y-\mathbf py−p
p−y\mathbf p-\mathbf yp−y
p(1−p)\mathbf p(1-\mathbf p)p(1−p)
−log⁡p-\log\mathbf p−logp

logistic-regression.prompt: Why don't we train classifiers by directly maximizing accuracy?
logistic-regression.explanation: Cross-entropy is a smooth, convex surrogate that also rewards calibrated confidence.
options: Accuracy is piecewise constant, so its gradient is zero almost everywhere
Accuracy is always 100% on training data
Accuracy is not defined for two classes
It would be too slow to compute

logistic-regression.explanation: It applies a numerically stable log-softmax internally; feeding softmax outputs double-applies it.

logistic-regression.prompt: Logistic regression's decision boundary w⊤x=0\mathbf w^\top\mathbf x=0w⊤x=0 is…
logistic-regression.explanation: The model is linear in its inputs, so the 0.5-probability boundary is linear.

knn-nb.prompt: What is the "naive" assumption in Naive Bayes?
knn-nb.explanation: It lets p(x∣y)p(\mathbf x\mid y)p(x∣y) factor into a product of one-dimensional terms.
options: Features are conditionally independent given the class

knn-nb.prompt: Why compute Naive Bayes scores as sums of logs?
knn-nb.explanation: A product of hundreds of probabilities underflows to 0 in floating point; a sum of logs does not.
options: To avoid numerical underflow from multiplying many small probabilities
Logs make the model more accurate
It is required for Laplace smoothing

knn-nb.prompt: Increasing kkk in k-NN generally…
knn-nb.explanation: Averaging over more neighbours smooths predictions. k-NN has no training step; prediction cost grows instead.
options: gives smoother decision boundaries with lower variance and higher bias

svm.prompt: Which training points determine an SVM's decision boundary?
svm.explanation: In the dual solution only points with αi>0\alpha_i\gt0αi​>0 contribute: the support vectors.
options: The support vectors, on or inside the margin
The points farthest from the boundary

svm.prompt: What is the margin width of a hard-margin SVM in terms of w\mathbf ww?
svm.explanation: The distance from the hyperplane to each margin is 1/∥w∥1/\|\mathbf w\|1/∥w∥, so the full width is 2/∥w∥2/\|\mathbf w\|2/∥w∥.
options: ∥w∥\|\mathbf w\|∥w∥
1/∥w∥1/\|\mathbf w\|1/∥w∥
2/∥w∥2/\|\mathbf w\|2/∥w∥
∥w∥2\|\mathbf w\|^2∥w∥2

svm.prompt: The kernel trick lets an SVM work in a high-dimensional feature space without computing the features explicitly.
svm.explanation: Predictions only need dot products, which a kernel K(x,x′)=ϕ(x)⊤ϕ(x′)K(\mathbf x,\mathbf x')=\phi(\mathbf x)^\top\phi(\mathbf x')K(x,x′)=ϕ(x)⊤ϕ(x′) supplies directly.

svm.prompt: Increasing the soft-margin parameter CCC…
svm.explanation: Large CCC fits the training data more tightly; small CCC allows more violations for a wider margin.
options: penalizes margin violations more, lowering bias and raising variance

trees-ensembles.prompt: A node contains 6 positives and 4 negatives. What is its Gini impurity?
trees-ensembles.explanation: 1−(0.62+0.42)=1−0.52=0.481-(0.6^2+0.4^2)=1-0.52=0.481−(0.62+0.42)=1−0.52=0.48.

trees-ensembles.prompt: How does a random forest reduce the correlation between its trees?
trees-ensembles.explanation: Lower correlation ρ\rhoρ makes the ρσ2\rho\sigma^2ρσ2 term of the ensemble variance smaller.
options: By training each tree on the same data
By bootstrap sampling and considering a random subset of features at each split
By pruning every tree to depth 1

trees-ensembles.prompt: In gradient boosting with squared loss, each new tree is fit to…
trees-ensembles.explanation: The pseudo-residuals −∂L/∂F-\partial\mathcal L/\partial F−∂L/∂F equal y−Fy-Fy−F for squared loss: gradient descent in function space.
options: the residuals of the current model
the predictions of the previous tree

trees-ensembles.prompt: Lowering the boosting learning rate (shrinkage) usually requires more trees but generalizes better.
trees-ensembles.explanation: Smaller steps reduce overfitting to each tree; early stopping on validation picks the number of trees.

unsupervised.explanation: Maximizing u⊤Σu\mathbf u^\top\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf uu⊤Σu subject to ∥u∥=1\|\mathbf u\|=1∥u∥=1 gives Σu=λu\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf u=\lambda\mathbf uΣu=λu with the largest λ\lambdaλ.
options: the eigenvector of the covariance matrix with the largest eigenvalue
the feature with the largest mean
the first column of the data

unsupervised.prompt: Which statements about k-means are true? (select all)
unsupervised.explanation: Lloyd's algorithm is monotone but local; k-means++ initialization and several restarts are standard.
options: Each iteration cannot increase the objective
It can converge to a local optimum, so restarts help
It always finds the global optimum
It is a hard-assignment limit of a Gaussian mixture with equal spherical covariances

unsupervised.prompt: Distances between far-apart clusters in a t-SNE plot reliably show how different those clusters are.
unsupervised.explanation: t-SNE preserves local neighbourhoods; global distances and cluster sizes are not meaningful.

unsupervised.prompt: In EM for Gaussian mixtures, what does the E-step compute?
unsupervised.explanation: The M-step then re-estimates parameters from those responsibilities.
options: Responsibilities: soft assignments of points to components

metrics.prompt: 1,000 transactions contain 10 frauds. A model flags 20 and catches 8. What is its precision?
For the same model, what is its recall?

metrics.explanation: This ranking interpretation makes AUC threshold-free.
options: a random positive is scored higher than a random negative

metrics.explanation: Calibration is about trusting the probabilities themselves; check it with a reliability diagram.
options: among predictions of 0.8, about 80% are positive

time-series.prompt: How should you validate a forecasting model?
time-series.explanation: Shuffling lets the model peek at the future, which inflates scores.
options: Backtesting: train on the past, test on the following window, then roll forward

time-series.prompt: Why compute rolling-mean features on y.shift(1) rather than on y?
time-series.explanation: Without the shift, the target leaks into its own feature.
options: So today's feature does not include today's target value

time-series.prompt: MASE compares a model's error with that of a seasonal-naive forecast. A MASE of 0.8 means…
time-series.explanation: MASE below 1 beats the naive baseline; above 1 loses to it.
options: the model's error is 20% lower than the naive forecast's
the model is worse than naive

time-series.prompt: Which loss trains a model to predict the 90th percentile?
time-series.explanation: The asymmetric pinball loss makes under-prediction 9 times costlier than over-prediction at τ=0.9\tau=0.9τ=0.9.
options: The pinball (quantile) loss with τ=0.9\tau=0.9τ=0.9

recsys.prompt: Why do large recommenders use a multi-stage funnel?
recsys.explanation: Candidate generation (two-tower + ANN) trims millions of items to hundreds, which a rich ranker can afford.
options: A heavy ranking model is too slow to score every item, so cheap retrieval narrows candidates first

recsys.prompt: The BPR loss for implicit feedback trains the model to…
recsys.explanation: −log⁡σ(r^ui−r^uj)-\log\sigma(\hat r_{ui}-\hat r_{uj})−logσ(r^ui​−r^uj​) optimizes pairwise ranking.
options: rank an observed item above a sampled unobserved one

recsys.prompt: Which problems are specific to recommenders? (select all)
recsys.explanation: Each requires dedicated handling: content features, exploration, and debiasing.
options: Cold start for new users and items
Feedback loops: the model learns only from what it showed

bayesian-ml.prompt: Bayesian linear regression's posterior mean equals which estimator?
bayesian-ml.explanation: A Gaussian prior on weights gives the ridge solution; the posterior adds a variance on top.
options: Ridge regression with λ=α/β\lambda=\alpha/\betaλ=α/β

bayesian-ml.prompt: Which uncertainty shrinks as you collect more data?
bayesian-ml.explanation: Epistemic uncertainty comes from lack of data; aleatoric is noise in the data itself.

bayesian-ml.prompt: Exact Gaussian process regression scales as…
bayesian-ml.explanation: Inverting the n×nn\times nn×n kernel matrix costs cubic time, which is why sparse approximations exist.
options: O(n)O(n)O(n)
O(nlog⁡n)O(n\log n)O(nlogn)
O(n3)O(n^3)O(n3)
O(1)O(1)O(1)

bayesian-ml.prompt: Deep ensembles estimate uncertainty from the disagreement between independently trained networks.
bayesian-ml.explanation: Train several seeds; where they disagree, the prediction is uncertain. Simple and effective in practice.

hpo.prompt: Why does random search usually beat grid search for the same budget?
hpo.explanation: With a grid, most trials repeat the same values of the important parameter.
options: Each random trial tries a new value of every hyperparameter, including the few that matter
Random numbers are faster to compute

hpo.prompt: Learning rates and regularization strengths should be searched on a log scale.
hpo.explanation: Their effect spans orders of magnitude, so 1e-4 vs 1e-3 matters as much as 1e-2 vs 1e-1.

hpo.prompt: What does Hyperband / successive halving do?
hpo.explanation: Multi-fidelity search spends compute on promising configurations.
options: Starts many configurations on small budgets and promotes only the best to larger ones
Halves the learning rate every epoch

causal.prompt: Users of feature X retain 20% better. Why can't you conclude X causes retention?
causal.explanation: Only a randomized experiment, or careful adjustment for confounders, identifies the causal effect.
options: Engaged users may both adopt X and retain better: a confounder

causal.prompt: Roughly how many users per group detect a 1-point lift from a 10% conversion rate at 5% significance and 80% power? (nearest thousand)
causal.explanation: n≈7.85⋅2⋅0.09/0.012≈14,100n\approx7.85\cdot2\cdot0.09/0.01^2\approx14{,}100n≈7.85⋅2⋅0.09/0.012≈14,100.

causal.prompt: Stopping an A/B test the first time the p-value drops below 0.05 inflates the false-positive rate.
causal.explanation: Repeated peeking gives many chances to cross the threshold by luck; use a fixed horizon or sequential tests.
Lower variance means smaller samples detect the same effect.
options: Reduces metric variance using each user's pre-experiment data

__exam.prompt: You need a strong first model for a tabular churn dataset with 200k rows, mixed feature types and missing values. What do you start with?
__exam.explanation: GBDTs handle mixed types, missing values and interactions with little tuning; a linear baseline tells you how much they add.
options: Gradient-boosted trees, after a logistic-regression baseline

__exam.prompt: Your fraud model's ROC-AUC is 0.97 but analysts say most flagged cases are legitimate. What explains it?
__exam.explanation: Look at precision–recall and tune the threshold for the review capacity.
options: With rare positives, even a low false-positive rate produces many false alarms, so precision is low

__exam.prompt: Which techniques give probability estimates you can use for decisions? (select all)
__exam.explanation: SVM margins are scores, not probabilities, unless calibrated.
options: Calibrated gradient boosting (e.g. isotonic or Platt scaling)

__exam.prompt: A model trained on randomly split time-series data scores far better offline than in production. Most likely cause?
__exam.explanation: Use time-based backtesting so the model never sees the future during validation.
options: Leakage of future information through the random split

__exam.prompt: In gradient boosting, decreasing the learning rate from 0.3 to 0.03 should be paired with…
__exam.explanation: Smaller steps need more of them to reach the same fit.
options: more trees, chosen by early stopping
